propositions: Finding text longer than 240 characters is silently clipped mid-sentence with no ellipsis or marker, making the truncation invisible to the change author.
When more than 10 blocking findings exist, excess findings are silently dropped with no '(N more)' disclosure note, causing the comment to understate the scope of required fixes.
The Gerrit comment header claims the total number of blocking findings but the body only shows truncated top-10, violating the actionable feedback contract for blocked changes.
The codebase already establishes a truncation marker convention (voter.py:440 uses '… n unchanged line(s) …'), making the silent clipping in adapter.py inconsistent with established patterns.
Full finding details must remain discoverable and the comment must explicitly disclose when truncation or omission has occurred.
